headline: CoreWeave beat sparks chip rally, Arm up 12.1 and Micron 11.9 percent, as dollar hits 52-week high
subhead: S&P 500 rose 1.3 percent to 7,619.4 and Nasdaq 1.6 percent as Micron gained 11.9 and Arm 12.1, while the 10-year yield held at 5.0 percent and gold fell 1.0 percent to 3,989.1.

us.text: S&P 500 rose 1.3 percent to 7,619.4 and Nasdaq 1.6 percent to 25,466.2 as CoreWeave's beat and raised outlook eased AI spending worries.
Rates still bite: hot October CPI and Waller floating a half-point December hike kept the 10-year yield at 5.0 percent.
Ahead: jobless claims plus Cisco and Applied Materials results on 12 November, PPI on 13 November, Nvidia results on 17 November.

india.text: Nifty rose 0.1 percent to 25,044.7 and Bank Nifty 1.1 percent to 59,741.3 on 9 November, led by PSU banks while IT lagged.
FIIs net bought Rs 12,563 crore and DIIs net sold Rs 8,435 crore on 11 November, per NSE provisional data.
USD/INR at 93.92 keeps the rupee near seven-month highs on foreign portfolio inflows and lower crude.

global.text: Asia: Kospi rose 2.5 percent and Nikkei 1.4 percent to 61,301 as Samsung, SK hynix and Japanese chipmakers rallied.
Europe closed higher on 11 November as an AI and chip rebound lifted tech, with Germany leading.
Dollar index rose 0.6 percent to 102.8, a 52-week high, as December Fed hike odds reached 87 percent; yen near 160.

calendar.what: India October CPI; US weekly jobless claims; UK third quarter GDP; Cisco and Applied Materials results after the US close
US IPOs expected: Rezera (RZRA) Nasdaq debut; vVardis (VVVV) pricing with NYSE trading 13 November; Windward Bio (WWB) pricing (dates provisional)
Japan third quarter preliminary GDP (sources differ on the date)
China October industrial output and retail sales; Baidu and Tyson Foods results
NVIDIA third quarter results; US October retail sales
Anthropic IPO pricing possible per Renaissance Capital, first trade reported for 19 or 20 November; no price range filed

weekly.narrative: The US midterms set the tone: a relief rally on Wednesday gave way to Thursday's AI chip rout on fears a Democratic Congress curbs data center building, and Friday's partial rebound and a 165,000 payrolls beat still left the S&P 500 down 2.7 percent and the Nasdaq 3.4 percent on the week. India went the other way, with foreign buying and cheaper crude lifting the Nifty 8.6 percent on the week and above 25,000 on Friday, while Kospi and the Nikkei bore the brunt of the chip selloff. Hopes of an Iran deal drove WTI down 12.8 percent on the week, and gold rose 4.5 percent and silver 5.5 percent despite rising Fed hike bets, while Bitcoin slipped 3.4 percent. Next week brings US CPI on 10 November, India CPI on 12 November, China's rare earth export pause expiring and a reported start to Anthropic's IPO roadshow.
